title: Willie Lewis's cable and the decision to go to Europe
summary: Domestic troubles and Willie Lewis's invitation led Carter to leave for Paris with his daughter, thinking of staying permanently.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I received a cable from Willie Lewis, who was leading a band in Paris at a club called the "Che France" and he asked me if I would like to join the band. I was having a little difficulty in New York at the time, particularly domestic difficulty, and I decided it might be a very, very good opportunity to get away from a lot of hassling for awhile and also to get to Europe, which I felt that I would be interested in seeing Paris and you know?
Right. At that time, how long did you think you might be away? I mean what was the time frame of this whole idea?

Well, in all honesty, I wasn't sure, but I guess that when I made up my mind to go, I probably had the idea of staying forever because I took my young daughter with me, who had been in custody of my wife, and I was very, very angry about this, and I wanted her with me.
I should say had been given to --
And so I suppose that I just went with the idea of staying; I didn't know when I would come back, and I didn't even think of it at that moment.
I see. So this could have been for you a permanent change. If things went well, you were
Well, at that point, yes. If someone had offered me a 20 year contract, I probably would have signed it.
